title: Core and --json: read bd and herdr, emit the contract
description:
Effort slug: `core-json`

> The roster below is authoritative. The first note on this bead carries an
> earlier roster written before the prep review; it is superseded and its
> collision warning is wrong.

## Goal

A `bdi --json` binary that reads one or more beads trackers and, where
available, a herdr session, and emits a tree of work per root annotated with
the live agent on each node. The TUI and the Noctalia widget are out of scope
and get their own plans.

## The plan

`docs/plans/2026-08-30-core-and-json.md`, ten tasks. `docs/design.md` is the
spec and is accepted; where the plan and the design disagree, the design wins.

**The plan has a Known defects section at its end.** Each entry names the task
it lands in, and every one has been folded into the relevant bead. A worker
that implements its plan task verbatim will reproduce a known bug. **Read the
bead's corrections before the plan's code.**

## Roster

Eleven beads, all in this tracker. No foreign strands, no tracking beads.

| bead | task | blocked by |
|---|---|---|
| bdi-3um.1 | T1 scaffold the crate, extending the existing dev shell | — |
| bdi-3um.2 | T2 configuration, with the per-project credential command | .1 |
| bdi-3um.3 | T3 parse bd's dependency-tree JSON | .1 |
| bdi-3um.5 | T5 parse herdr's agent list | .1 |
| bdi-3um.4 | T4 assemble and order the tree | .3 |
| bdi-3um.6 | T6 join agents onto beads, scoped by project | .2 .4 .5 |
| bdi-3um.9 | T9 run bd and herdr per project, per-project credential | .2 .5 |
| bdi-3um.7 | T7 anomaly rules, every rule that fires | .6 |
| bdi-3um.8 | T8 assemble the snapshot, counts, live-agent filter | .7 |
| bdi-3um.10 | T10 wire the binary and emit the JSON contract | .8 .9 |
| bdi-3um.11 | T11 discovery rule 4: roots named only by a live pane | .10 |

`.11` did not exist in the plan. It was split out of `.10` during prep, which
was carrying app wiring, discovery, a snapshot-type change and an integration
test in one bead.

## Critical path and parallel windows

`.1` → `.3` → `.4` → `.6` → `.7` → `.8` → `.10` → `.11`.

- After `.1`: **`.2`, `.3` and `.5` all open at once.**
- `.9` opens as soon as `.2` and `.5` are done and runs alongside the whole
  `.6` → `.7` → `.8` chain. That is the effort's one long parallel strand.

`.5` deliberately does **not** block on `.3`, despite the plan's numbering. It
consumes nothing from it; the only coupling is a two-line `src/collect/mod.rs`.

## Delivery mode: direct push

`main` on `github.com/CodeForBreakfast/beady-eye` reports `protected: false`
and has no rulesets. **Beads close on push, not on merge.** No PR-ordering
edges are wired, because there is no review tower to prevent.

## File collisions to expect — two, both one line

- `src/lib.rs`: `.2` and `.3` each append a `pub mod` line, and they run
  concurrently.
- `src/collect/mod.rs`: `.3` and `.5` — whichever lands first creates it, the
  other appends.

`.4`, `.6`, `.7` and `.8` all touch `src/model/mod.rs` but form a strict chain
and can never run concurrently, so that is not a collision.

**`.8` and `.9` do run concurrently and both need `TrackerState`'s unreachable
reason.** That is resolved by ownership, not by an edge: `.9` detects failures
in its own `collect/run.rs`, `.8` defines the representation in `snapshot.rs`,
and `.10` maps between them. Neither reaches into the other's file.

## Facts verified against a live tracker during prep

Run against this repo's own tracker on 2026-08-30. These override any
contradicting reading of `docs/design.md`'s data-sources table.

- **`bd dep tree --json` omits every empty field.** `edge_from_parent`,
  `metadata`, `closed_at` and `close_reason` are *absent*, not null, when
  empty. `started_at` and `assignee` were never observed at all. A parser
  written against one row shape breaks on the first real tracker.
- **`metadata` is inline per row** — confirmed on a bead carrying
  `agent_pane`. The design is right: badges need no second call.
- **`blocked_by` is NOT recoverable from `bd dep tree`.** A node with two
  blockers appears once, under one of them; the other is absent entirely.
  `bd blocked --json` is the source — it returns `blocked_by: [ids]` and
  `blocked_by_count`. `.9` delivers it, `.8` consumes it.
- **Sibling order from bd is arbitrary.** The root's children came back
  `.10, .7, .2, .5, .3, .1`. Re-ordering in `.4` is load-bearing.
- `bdi-5yq`, the closed smoke-test bead, carries an `agent_pane` metadata key
  set during this probe so a metadata-bearing row can be captured for a
  fixture.

## One decision made during prep, open to reversal

`docs/design.md` says the four join disagreements are *reported*, but its JSON
contract has nowhere to put them — so as written `.6` computes findings that
`.8` drops. They are now carried as a top-level **`conflicts`** list on the
snapshot, mirroring `unattributed`, which is the existing precedent for a
finding belonging to no tree. If Graeme wants a different shape, this is the
thing to change.

## Global constraints, on every bead

- **Never write to bd.** Only `list`, `show`, `dep tree`, `ready`, `blocked`.
  Only `herdr agent list` / `read` / `get`.
- **The key is `(project, id)`, never `id` alone.** Prefixes are per-tracker
  and uncoordinated.
- **Degrade, never disappear.** An unreachable tracker, a dangling parent, a
  truncated subtree, a filtered tree — each is reported, never dropped.
- **`--limit 0` on every `bd list`.** The default is 50 and truncation
  silently changes meaning.
- **herdr's `agent_status` is a terminal property**, never a bead status and
  never a badge.
- **Fail loudly on an unexpected JSON shape.** A field of the wrong type is an
  error; a *missing* field is normal — see the omitempty finding above.
- **TDD with a real red phase.** Write the test, watch it fail for the right
  reason, then implement. Missing module wiring is not a red phase.

## Working in this repo

`nix develop` (or direnv) — it pins bd 1.2.2 and scopes `BEADS_DIR`. A bare
`bd` from an ambient shell may resolve a different binary or another project's
tracker. See `CLAUDE.md`.

**This epic appears in `bd ready` alongside `.1`.** It is the anchor, not work;
do not staff it.

## Why the edges are where they are

- `.5` blocks on `.3` rather than on `.1` because it modifies
  `src/collect/mod.rs`, which `.3` creates.
- `.9` blocks on `.5` and `.2`, not on the T6/T7/T8 chain: it modifies
  `collect/bd.rs` and `collect/herdr.rs` and needs `Project::credential_command`.
  It runs alongside that chain, which is the effort's one long parallel strand.
- `.7` blocks only on `.6`; its need for `config::Anomalies` is covered
  transitively.
- No PR-ordering edges. `main` is unprotected, so beads close on push and there
  is no review tower to prevent.

## Two file-level collisions to expect, both trivial

`.2` and `.3` each add one `pub mod` line to `src/lib.rs`; `.4`, `.6`, `.7` and
`.8` each add one to `src/model/mod.rs`. Where two land close together, the
second rebases through a one-line conflict. Expected, not a defect.
Prep review applied. The roster in the first note above is superseded by the description: .11 was added, .5 was re-parented from .3 to .1, and that note's src/model/mod.rs collision warning is wrong (.4/.6/.7/.8 are a strict chain and never run concurrently).
Two things a cold orchestrator needs that the description does not say:

**Use `bd ready --exclude-type=epic` when looking for spawnable work.** This
epic is unblocked and so appears in a bare `bd ready` alongside bdi-3um.1. It
is the anchor, not work. Setting it in_progress on bind also removes it.

**The effort's own deferred risk has a bead, and it is not a child of this
one:** bdi-vx7, proving the per-project credential against a live second
tracker. bdi-3um.9 tests that path against a fake only, by design. bdi-vx7 is
deliberately outside this effort because it is blocked on a cross-project
consent decision that is Graeme's to make. Do not staff it.
Correction to this bead's 'Facts verified against a live tracker' section, from bdi-3um.3's capture on 2026-08-30: assignee and started_at ARE present on every claimed bead, contrary to 'never observed at all' above. Both stay optional, so no design change — but they are not hypothetical and Task 7's age rules and Task 8's emission both want them. Also: parent_id is an empty string on the root, not absent; bdi-3um.3 normalises it to None at the parse boundary.

title: T10 wire the binary and emit the JSON contract
description:
Plan: Task 10, `docs/plans/2026-08-30-core-and-json.md:1990`.

**Deliverable:** `app::run`, `root_of`, the per-project loop, `bdi --json`,
`bdi --config <path>`, `bdi --all`, and `tests/snapshot_json.rs`.

**Discovery rule 4 is not in this bead** — it is bdi-3um.11, which depends on
this one. Implement rules 1 to 3 here and leave the seam for it.

## What this bead wires together

- Per project: build the environment from `credential_command` (bdi-3um.2),
  run the collectors (bdi-3um.9), and map a `collect::run` failure onto the
  `TrackerState` reason that bdi-3um.8 defines. **This mapping is this bead's
  job** — `.8` and `.9` deliberately never touch each other's files.
- Feed `ready_ids` and `blocked_by` from bdi-3um.9 into `build_tree`. Those
  are the only sources; nothing infers readiness or a blocker set.
- Emit the contract.

## Known defect to fix as you reach it

**`the_json_carries_the_contract_fields` asserts key presence only**, so nulls
and wrong enum spellings pass. Assert values.

## Definition of done

- `bdi --json` emits the contract in `docs/design.md` — `generated_at`,
  `herdr`, `filter`, `trees`, `hidden_trees`, `unattributed` — plus the
  top-level `conflicts` list that bdi-3um.8 adds so the join findings have
  somewhere to go.
- `agent.source` records which direction of the join resolved each agent;
  `herdr` is `ok` or `unavailable` so a consumer knows which tier it reads.
- A project whose tracker is unreachable renders as its own failure, named,
  with its live panes — not as an anonymous empty tree, and two such failures
  stay distinguishable.
- Roots come from bd, unioned and deduped across discovery rules 1 to 3.
- **Still true at the end:** the binary never writes to bd. No bd subcommand
  beyond `list`, `show`, `dep tree`, `ready`, `blocked`; no herdr subcommand
  beyond `agent list`. `agent focus` belongs to the TUI, not here.
- A real red phase, then implement.
- Committed and pushed.

title: T11 discovery rule 4: roots named only by a live pane
description:
Split out of bdi-3um.10 during prep, which was carrying too much for one
context. This is new work — the plan's Task 10 does not implement it and does
not consult `panes` at all. Its self-review claimed full spec coverage and was
wrong.

**Deliverable:** the fourth root source in `docs/design.md`'s Discovery
section — a bead named by a live pane's `display_agent` that rules 1 to 3
missed, unioned and deduped into the root set.

## Why it exists

So an agent working off-tree still appears. It is the only root herdr
contributes; every other root comes from bd, which is deliberate — an earlier
draft had herdr enumerate the roots and that drops any root with no pane,
silently and with concrete evidence behind it.

## Watch for

- `display_agent` is **free text**. Any string an agent stamps lands there, so
  parsing it as a bead id is a heuristic and must fail soft: a value that is
  not a resolvable bead id contributes no root and is not an error.
- The pane must resolve to a project first (bdi-3um.6's rule), and the root it
  contributes belongs to that project. `(project, id)`, never id alone.

## Definition of done

- A pane whose `display_agent` names a bead no other rule found produces that
  bead's root in the output.
- A pane whose `display_agent` is not a bead id changes nothing and raises
  nothing.
- **Still true:** rules 1 to 3 produce the same roots they did before, and a
  root with no pane at all still appears.
- A real red phase, then implement.
- Committed and pushed.

title: T3 parse bd's dependency-tree JSON
description:
Plan: Task 3, `docs/plans/2026-08-30-core-and-json.md:354`.

**Deliverable:** `model::types::{Bead, Status, Edge}`,
`collect::bd::parse_dep_tree`, and the `tests/fixtures/bd_dep_tree.json`
fixture.

## Verified against the live tracker, 2026-08-30

`bd dep tree <root> --direction=up --json` was run against this repo's own
tracker. Do not design the parser from `docs/design.md`'s field table alone —
it is close but not exact. What is actually there:

`created_at`, `created_by`, `depth`, `description`, `id`, `issue_type`,
`notes`, `owner`, `parent_id`, `priority`, `status`, `title`, `truncated`,
`updated_at`, plus `edge_from_parent`, `metadata`, `closed_at` and
`close_reason` **when non-empty**.

**Every optional field is omitempty — absent, not null.** Observed absent:
`edge_from_parent` on the root row, `metadata` on a bead with none,
`closed_at` and `close_reason` on anything not closed. `started_at` and
`assignee` were never observed at all; treat both as optional and do not
assume they exist.

This is the parse hazard for this task. "Fail loudly on an unexpected shape"
means a field of the **wrong type** is an error; a field that is simply
**missing** is normal and must deserialise to `None`.

**`metadata` is inline per row** — confirmed with a bead carrying
`agent_pane`. The design is right that badges need no second call.

## Known defect to fix as you reach it

**Unknown enum values are untested.** `Status::Other` and `Edge::Other` exist
so a new bd value does not break the parse, and nothing round-trips one. Feed
an unrecognised status and an unrecognised edge and assert they land in
`Other`. This is about compatibility with a future bd, not serde syntax.

## Definition of done

- `Bead` carries `issue_type` and, as options, `started_at` and `closed_at` —
  the JSON contract needs them and Task 8 cannot emit what is not parsed here.
- The fixture exercises **both shapes of every optional field**: a root row
  with no `edge_from_parent`, a child with one; a row with `metadata` and a row
  without; a closed row with `closed_at` and an open row without. A fixture
  where every row is the same shape produces a parser that breaks on the first
  real tracker.
- `truncated` is carried through, not ignored — a truncated node means the tree
  is incomplete, which is the silent partial answer this tool exists to avoid.
- A field of the wrong type is an error, not a default.
- Committed and pushed.

## Capturing fixtures

From *this machine's own* trackers only. `bdi-5yq` in this tracker carries an
`agent_pane` metadata key, set during prep precisely so a metadata-bearing row
can be captured; it is the closed smoke-test bead and exists to be poked.

title: T4 assemble and order the tree
description:
Plan: Task 4, `docs/plans/2026-08-30-core-and-json.md:570`.

**Deliverable:** `model::tree::{Placed, Assembled, assemble}` — rows into a
renderable structure by `parent_id`, siblings re-ordered, depth recomputed
from the parent chain.

bd has already resolved and deduped the tree, so this assembles rows; it does
not walk edges.

## Known defects to fix as you reach them

**`assemble` silently keeps only the last root.** `None => root = Some(bead)`
overwrites. Valid `bd dep tree` output has exactly one root — validate that
and fail loudly rather than discarding components.

**Unreachable rows are dropped.** Rows not reached by the traversal must be
reported alongside `dangling`. Degrade, never disappear, applies to them too.

## Three tests that would pass against a wrong implementation

Fix these as you write them, not after:

- `depth_is_recomputed_from_the_parent_chain` — the plan's fixture already
  carries the expected `depth` values, so simply copying bd's `depth` passes.
  Give the fixture deliberately wrong depths.
- `a_parent_cycle_terminates` — `b` and `c` are disconnected, so `walk` never
  reaches them and the `seen` guard is never exercised. Wire the cycle into
  the reachable graph.
- `siblings_order_...` — it tests the status rank and neither the priority nor
  the id tie-break. Assert all three.

## Definition of done

- `assemble` returns `Assembled { rows, dangling, unreachable }` from a flat
  `Vec<Bead>`: one row per bead, in render order, each with a depth recomputed
  from its parent chain rather than copied from bd.
- **Sibling order is state, then priority, then id** — in-flight, then
  blocked, then open, then closed; then priority; then id. All three tie-breaks
  asserted.
- Exactly one root, or a loud failure.
- A parent id naming a bead not in the input is reported as `dangling`, never
  dropped; a row the traversal never reaches is reported as `unreachable`.
- A cycle in the parent chain terminates rather than hanging.
- A real red phase: write the test, watch it fail *for the right reason*, then
  implement. Missing module wiring is not a red phase.
- Committed and pushed.

## Note on the real data

`bd dep tree` returns rows in a valid pre-order but with **arbitrary sibling
order** — verified on this repo's own tracker, where the root's children came
back `.10, .7, .2, .5, .3, .1`. Re-ordering is the whole point of this bead;
do not assume bd's order is already what you want.
notes: From bdi-3um.3's live capture, 2026-08-30: bd emits parent_id as an EMPTY STRING on the root row, not as an absent field. docs/design.md:203 says the same. bdi-3um.3 normalises empty-string to None at the parse boundary, so this bead should never see Some(""). If it ever does, the root gets filed as a dangling parent — that is the bug this note exists to prevent. Do not re-add a plain Option<String> passthrough.

title: T1 scaffold the crate, extending the existing dev shell
description:
Plan: Task 1, `docs/plans/2026-08-30-core-and-json.md:25`.

**Deliverable:** crate `beady_eye` (lib) plus binary `bdi`, building and
testing under the existing dev shell. Every later task adds modules under
`src/`.

## Two corrections to the plan, both load-bearing

**Extend `flake.nix`; do not create it.** The plan says "Create: flake.nix"
and gives a bare Rust shell. `flake.nix` already exists and carries the beads
1.2.2 pin, `BEADS_DIR`, `BD_SMART_GATE=0` and the `.env.local` sourcing.
Replacing it breaks the tracker for every session. Add cargo, rustc, rustfmt,
clippy and rust-analyzer to the existing `buildInputs`, and add the
`packages.default` rustPlatform derivation alongside the existing devShell. Do
not add `inputs.nixpkgs.follows` to the beads input — the flake's own comment
says why.

**Do not create `rust-toolchain.toml`.** The plan pins channel 1.83 there
while the shell supplies nixpkgs' rustc. There is no rustup on this machine,
so the file is inert at best, and actively fights the flake if rustup ever
lands on PATH. The flake is the pin.

## Definition of done

- `cargo test` passes `version_is_not_empty`.
- `cargo run` prints `bdi 0.1.0`.
- **Still works after the change:** `nix develop` prints the beads version and
  its resolved path, loads `.env.local`, and `bd list` reaches the tracker from
  inside the shell. Confirm this, don't assume it — the flake edit is the one
  place this effort can break the tracker it is tracked in.
- Committed and pushed.
close_reason: Crate scaffolded and pushed as 9dec128. cargo test passes version_is_not_empty, cargo run prints bdi 0.1.0, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check are clean. nix develop still prints beads 1.2.2 with its resolved store path, loads .env.local, and bd list reaches the tracker. nix build .#default produces a working bdi. flake.nix extended, not replaced; no rust-toolchain.toml.
